Legal proceedings against her are underway, he added.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir: Not Hasina, only winter will come in December
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Thursday said former prime minister Sheikh Hasina would not return to Bangladesh in December, humorously remarking that only winter is certain to arrive.
“I have already said at a meeting in Sylhet that Sheikh Hasina will not come in December……nobody will come in December; only winter will come,” he said, adding that her return, if it happens, would have to be through the extradition treaty.
Kobir said Hasina would have to be brought back through a formal handover, either in handcuffs aboard a plane or under strict surveillance. “This is the only way she can come back,” he said.
Responding to a question about remarks by some West Bengal ministers threatening to occupy Bangladesh on December 16, Kobir said political figures making such statements could be found everywhere.
“There are some crazy people in politics everywhere in the world. Our relationship will be with the central government of India,” he said.
Talking to reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kobir said Bangladesh wants Hasina and other individuals accused of committing crimes in the country to be handed over by India under the existing extradition treaty.
“Under the extradition treaty, she has to be handed over,” he said, stressing that the treaty distinguishes between ordinary civilian travellers and individuals accused of criminal offences.
“We have made our requests and placed them before the relevant authorities. So, let's see,” Kobir said.
He also mentioned individuals accused of involvement in the killing of Shaheed Sharif Osman Hadi, saying Bangladesh wanted them to be returned through the extradition process.
Describing Hasina as a criminal and a terrorist, Kobir said she had lost her political relevance and alleged that she had shown no remorse.
He claimed that Hasina's family and political associates, whom he accused of looting the country and committing acts of violence, had no place in Bangladesh anymore.
He urged journalists to keep the discussion focused on relations between the two central governments, saying serious bilateral matters are addressed at that level.
On Bangladesh's trade negotiations with the United States, Kobir said the tariff agreements had become a flagship political and economic agenda of the Trump administration.
He said Bangladesh had reservations about certain provisions and would raise issues it considered unjustified through negotiations with Washington.
“There is scope for discussion. We have the opportunity to build our case and negotiate on issues where we believe the provisions are unjustified,” he said.
Citing cotton as an example, Kobir said Bangladesh imports cotton from the United States, manufactures products locally and exports those products to the American market.
He said this could provide a basis for discussing tariff arrangements and other trade-related matters.
“Of course, we have reservations, and we will talk and negotiate with them,” he said, adding that Bangladesh would clearly explain which provisions it considered justified and which it did not.
He also noted that the US tariff policy was not directed solely at Bangladesh, as similar measures had affected many other countries.
Kobir said a public hearing scheduled for January 26 would provide Bangladesh with an opportunity to present its arguments on the issues.
For the 14 economies including Bnagladesh, the US Trade Representative (USTR) has determined that certain acts, policies, and practices which create, sustain, or contribute to structural excess capacity and production are unreasonable and burden or restrict US commerce.
The USTR said Bangladesh’s unreasonable acts, policies, and practices include (1) industrial plans to maintain and expand its manufacturing sector, particularly in key sectors; (2) production incentives to promote production and exports; (3) inadequate labor protections; (4) financial repression policies; and (5) failure to address global excess capacity and production, including through imports and foreign direct investment from non-market economies.
These acts, policies, and practices burden or restrict US commerce by (1) reducing commercial opportunities for US producers and exporters in Bangladesh and third-country markets; (2) harming the US economy by contributing to lost production, exports, jobs, and investment in the US manufacturing sector; and (3) increasing US economic security risks, including through reliance on NME inputs.
The USTR said this is especially true in the ready-made garment and apparel sector.

item.title: CMM Court crude bomb blast: Arrestee placed on three-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court has placed Md Delwar Hossain on a three-day remand in a case filed over a crude bomb explosion on the premises of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Court in the capital.
On Thursday night, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Jashita Islam passed the order following a police application. State lawyer Shamsuddoha Sumon confirmed the matter.
The investigation officer of the case, Sub-Inspector (SI) Md Abdur Rahman of Kotwali police station, produced Delwar before the court and sought a 5-day remand.
In the remand application, the investigation officer said preliminary investigations had found information and evidence of Delwar's involvement in the incident.
He said Delwar needed to be interrogated to identify and arrest others involved in the incident, trace the collection of materials and equipment used to make explosives, and identify the financiers, advisers and those who gave instructions.
The application also stated that Delwar's mobile phone, which was used at the time of the incident, had not been recovered. The officer said recovering the phone could provide important information about the incident.
During the hearing, state lawyer Shamsuddoha Sumon argued in favor of the remand. No lawyer appeared on behalf of Delwar.
At one stage, the judge asked Delwar why he had come to the court. He replied that he had come to Courtroom No 9 of the CMM Court in connection with a land-related case and was sitting inside the courtroom when the crude bomb exploded.
Asked about his mobile phone, Delwar said he could not remember exactly whom he had given it to amid the situation following the explosion. However, he said he had handed his wallet to lawyer Mashiur Ahmed Mishu.
He also told the court that he had been unable to contact his family despite trying.
Earlier, before the judge entered the courtroom, the state lawyer had asked Delwar about his profession. He introduced himself as a contractor and said he had come to court in connection with a land-related case.
At the time, Delwar said he had been under mental pressure throughout the day and had to stand in the dock because he had talked too much.
The crude bomb exploded in front of the CMM Court building at around 11:18am on Thursday. Lawyer Hridoy Mia was injured in the incident. His colleagues later rescued him and took him to National Hospital.

item.title: Ex-MP Anar’s daughter Dorin placed on three-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Thursday placed Muntarin Ferdous Dorin, daughter of former Awami League MP Anwarul Azim Anar, on a three-day remand in an explosives case filed with Jatrabari police station.
The order was issued by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Hasan Sahadat after a hearing on Thursday afternoon. State counsel Shamsuddoha Sumon confirmed the matter.
Earlier, Sub-Inspector Md Shahadat Hossain Nafiz of the Detective Police's Wari Zonal Team, the investigation officer in the case, produced Dorin before the court and sought a 5-day remand.
According to the remand application, police needed to interrogate her to determine where the cocktails had been collected, identify other accused involved in the incident, and establish the identities and whereabouts of those who remain absconding.
During the hearing, state counsel Shamsuddoha Sumon argued that remand was necessary to identify and arrest unidentified accused, gather information about the explosives, and identify and apprehend the financiers and planners behind the incident.
He said a bomb explosion had occurred on the court premises that day and claimed there were links between the incidents. He also said Dorin was a front-line activist of Chhatra League and that her involvement in the incident had emerged during the investigation.
Opposing the remand, defence lawyer Farzana Yasmin Rakhi said her client was not named in the case and had been arrested as a suspect. She said Dorin was a law student and a victim of political vendetta, alleging that she was being harassed through a politically motivated case.
The defence lawyer also said Dorin was not involved in any activities against the country and requested the court to reject the remand application or, if necessary, allow police to question her at the jail gate.
After hearing both sides, the court granted Dorin a 3-day remand.
Dorin was arrested from the Lalmatia area of Mohammadpur in the capital on the night of November 25.
According to the case statement, unidentified miscreants detonated a cocktail on the paved road in front of the Kajla toll plaza on the Jatrabari-Demra road at around 11:15pm on November 9, triggering panic among the public and disrupting normal activities.
The statement alleges that the accused acted in collusion with one another and gathered at the scene to detonate the cocktail with the intention of deteriorating the country's law and order situation, creating anarchy and terror, and carrying out large-scale sabotage.
It further states that burnt parts of the cocktail, pieces of tin, 12 barbed-wire nails and a small piece of glass were recovered from the scene.
The case statement also describes the arrested accused as an active member and supporter of the Awami League and a banned organization, alleging involvement in a conspiracy to disrupt the country's sovereignty, public safety and law and order.
Police filed the case as the plaintiff in connection with the incident.

item.title: Vegetable prices stay high, eggs get costlier
item.description:
Vegetable prices remain high in Dhaka despite the arrival of winter produce, with most varieties selling for more than Tk80 per kg. Egg prices have also risen over the past week, while chicken has become slightly cheaper.
Traders attribute the high vegetable prices to recent rainfall, which damaged crops and disrupted supplies. Prices of domestic garlic have increased, although Chinese ginger and garlic have become cheaper. Overall, consumers continue to face pressure from high prices of essential commodities.
A visit to Mirpur-1 kitchen market on Thursday found most vegetables selling at elevated prices.
Local tomatoes were selling for Tk150 per kg, Indian tomatoes for Tk180 and green tomatoes for Tk80. Local carrots cost Tk100, while Chinese carrots were Tk140. New potatoes, both local and imported, were selling for Tk140 per kg.
Long aubergines cost Tk80, white round aubergines Tk100 and black round varieties Tk120. Beans were selling for Tk100-120, cucumbers Tk100, bitter gourd Tk100-110 and spiny gourd Tk160 per kg. Okra cost Tk80-100, pointed gourd Tk70-100, snake gourd, ridge gourd and sponge gourd Tk80 each, and yardlong beans Tk100.
Green chillies were selling for Tk80-100 per kg, coriander leaves for Tk160, hybrid cucumbers for Tk70, papaya for Tk40 and pumpkins for Tk50. Radishes cost Tk50 per kg, while cauliflower and cabbage were Tk60 each.
Vegetable trader Md Shah Alam said recent rain had damaged crops, pushing up prices, but expected them to fall in the coming days.
Another trader, Md Sohel, said a significant amount of produce had rotted during transportation and storage. He said 20 of the 130 cauliflowers he had brought to market had spoiled, forcing traders to raise prices to recover their losses.
Buyer Saidur Rahman said rising prices were making it increasingly difficult for people on fixed incomes to manage their household budgets.
Local onions were selling for Tk55 per kg, while hybrid varieties cost Tk50. Regular red and white potatoes were Tk25 per kg, while Bogra potatoes sold for Tk50.
Local garlic cost Tk110-120 per kg, Chinese garlic Tk150-160 and Chinese ginger Tk120-140. Local garlic prices rose by Tk10-20 per kg, while Chinese garlic fell by Tk10-20 and ginger by Tk20-30.
The price of red chicken eggs increased by Tk5-10 per dozen to Tk125-130, while white eggs sold for Tk120. Duck eggs rose by Tk20-30 to Tk200-210 per dozen.
Meanwhile, broiler chicken sold for Tk160-170 per kg, cock chicken for Tk280-300 and layer chicken for Tk287-290, down Tk7-20 per kg from the previous week. Local chicken remained expensive at Tk620-650 per kg.
Beef was selling for Tk800 per kg and mutton for Tk1,250.
Fish prices varied by size and quality. Ilish sold for Tk1,000-2,600 per kg, rohu for Tk400-700, catla for Tk350-600 and prawns for Tk700-1,600. Other varieties, including pabda, shing, tengra and boal, were selling at prices ranging from Tk400 to Tk1,200 per kg.
Prices of most grocery items remained unchanged, although cloves rose by Tk150 per kg and cumin by Tk140.
Packaged polao rice sold for Tk230 per kg, while loose varieties cost Tk160-180. Small lentils were Tk140-150 per kg, coarse lentils Tk90, chickpeas Tk120 and mung beans Tk140-170.
Bottled soybean oil cost Tk204 per litre, while loose soybean oil sold for Tk205 per kg and mustard oil for Tk220 per litre. Sugar remained Tk110 per kg, while packaged flour cost Tk170 for two kg and atta Tk140 for the same quantity.
Among spices, cardamom sold for Tk5,400 per kg, cinnamon for Tk500, cloves for Tk1,550 and cumin for Tk640.

item.title: Narayanganj seven-murder case hearing adjourned until December 8
item.description:
The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court has adjourned until December 8 the hearing on appeals against the High Court verdict in the case filed over the abduction and murder of 7 people, including Nazrul Islam, the then panel mayor of Narayanganj City Corporation, in 2014.
The Appellate Division, led by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, passed the order on Thursday after the second day of hearings.
Attorney General Ruhul Quddus Kazal and Additional Attorney General Anik Rushd Haque argued for the state, while senior lawyer SM Shahjahan represented the accused.
On April 27, 2014, 7 people, including Nazrul Islam, were abducted from the Lamapara area of Fatullah on the Dhaka-Narayanganj Link Road. Their bodies were recovered 3 days later.
The other victims were Nazrul Islam's friend Moniruzzaman Swapan, Tajul Islam, Liton, his driver Jahangir Alam, lawyer Chandan Kumar Sarkar and his driver Ibrahim.
Two murder cases were filed over the incident. Selina Islam Beauty, wife of Nazrul Islam, filed a case at Fatullah police station over the murders of Nazrul Islam and his 4 associates.
Meanwhile, son-in-law Bijoy Kumar Pal filed another case over the murders of lawyer Chandan Sarkar and his driver Ibrahim.
On January 16, 2017, the court of Narayanganj District and Sessions Judge Syed Enayet Hossain completed the trials of the 2 cases together and sentenced 26 people, including Nur Hossain and 3 former senior officials of Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) who had been dismissed from service, to death.
The remaining 9 accused were sentenced to different terms of imprisonment. The accused appealed against the verdict, while the case records were sent to the High Court for approval of the death sentences.
Hearings on the appeals and death references began at the High Court on May 22, 2017. After 33 working days of hearings, the High Court delivered its verdict on August 22, 2017.
The High Court upheld the death sentences of 15 of the 26 accused sentenced to death by the trial court and commuted the sentences of the remaining 11 to life imprisonment. It also upheld the prison terms of the remaining 9 accused.
Among the 15 accused whose death sentences were upheld were former Narayanganj City Corporation councillor Nur Hossain and 3 dismissed officials of Rab-11: former commander Lieutenant Colonel (retd) Tareque Sayeed Mohammad, Major (retd) Arif Hossain and Lieutenant Commander (retd) Masud Rana. The remaining 11 were also former members of Rab.
Among the 11 people sentenced to life imprisonment were former dismissed Rab constable Asaduzzaman Nur, Sergeant Enamul Kabir and 9 associates of Nur Hossain: Murtaza Zaman Churchill, Ali Mohammad, Mizanur Rahman Dipu, Abul Bashar, Raham Ali, Jamal Uddin Sardar, Selim, Sanaullah Sana and Shahjahan.
Of the 9 accused whose prison terms were upheld, the High Court upheld the 17-year sentence of Constable Habibur Rahman, the 10-year sentences of 7 people and the 7-year sentences of 2 people.
The accused later filed appeals against the High Court verdict with the Appellate Division.

item.title: Clash between police, workers in Gazipur; ASP injured
item.description:
A clash broke out between garment workers and police in Sreepur, Gazipur, on Thursday as workers blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in protest.
Several police personnel, including Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP) Md Shafiqul Islam of the Gazipur District Police's Kaliakair Circle, were injured.
The incident occurred around 11am in the Nayanpur area of Sreepur upazila.
According to police and eyewitnesses, workers from several nearby factories gathered in a procession and occupied part of the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway, bringing traffic to a standstill.
Police moved to clear the road and restore traffic, firing tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse the workers. During the confrontation, workers allegedly threw bricks at police, injuring ASP Shafiqul Islam and several other police personnel.
The situation has since stabilised, and traffic on the highway has returned to normal.
Md Nahid Niyaz Shishir, assistant commissioner (land) and executive magistrate of Sreepur upazila, confirmed the incident. He said law enforcement personnel intervened after workers blocked the highway around 11am, using tear gas to clear the road and restore traffic. He also confirmed that several police officers and personnel were injured by bricks thrown during the clash.
Meanwhile, amid the ongoing unrest, factories in several areas, including Konabari and Palli Bidyut in Gazipur, declared fresh closures on Thursday.
Factories in Bagher Bazar and Bhabanipur in Gazipur Sadar upazila, as well as Gargarhia Masterbari, Bairagir Chala and Kew in Sreepur upazila, have also announced a three-day holiday.
Law enforcement personnel remain on high alert at key points along the Dhaka-Tangail highway to prevent further incidents.

item.title: Community Bank to offer special loans for Police to buy Royal Enfield motorcycles
item.description:
Community Bank Bangladesh PLC has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with IFAD Motors Limited to introduce a special loan facility enabling members of Bangladesh Police to purchase Royal Enfield motorcycles, aiming to make their commuting easier and more comfortable.
IFAD Motors Limited is the sole manufacturer and distributor of Royal Enfield motorcycles in Bangladesh.
Under the arrangement, eligible police personnel will be able to borrow up to Tk250,000 to buy a Royal Enfield motorcycle.
The loan carries an interest rate of 9% and a repayment tenure of up to 10 years.
The facility will be available through both conventional banking and Islamic banking services.
Community Bank Bangladesh PLC managing director Mohammad Imtiaz Uddin attended the MoU signing ceremony, while IFAD Group was represented by vice chairman Taskeen Ahmed and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Mohammad Afsar Uddin.
Known globally for heritage, reliability and performance, Royal Enfield motorcycles are expected to add greater mobility to police personnel's personal travel and duty performance, with flexible financing terms making it more accessible for them to buy a bike of their choice.
Community Bank Bangladesh PLC has been providing need-based financial services to members of Bangladesh Police since its inception, and the agreement with IFAD Motors Limited marks a new addition to those ongoing efforts, expanding motorcycle ownership options for officers while serving as a notable example of corporate collaboration.
Through this initiative, Community Bank continues to tailor financial products toward the practical mobility and lifestyle needs of police personnel, pairing institutional support with commercial financing options offered alongside IFAD Motors.
By combining a decade-long repayment window with a 9 percent interest rate and dual conventional and Islamic banking access, the scheme is designed to ease upfront financial pressure while supporting everyday commuting and operational convenience for eligible members of the force.

item.title: Hitachi, Transcom digital unveil new refrigerator ranges at Hitachi Star Night 2026
item.description:
Hitachi has officially introduced its latest refrigerator ranges in Bangladesh at Hitachi Star Night 2026, an exclusive launch and press event hosted by its authorized partner, Transcom Digital, on Thursday, November 26, at Radisson Blu, Dhaka.
Celebrating excellence, shared success, and the launch of a new range of products, the event underscores Hitachi’s continued commitment to expanding its presence and strengthening its position in the Bangladesh market.
Drawing on more than a century of technological innovation and the heritage of Japanese craftsmanship, Hitachi’s latest refrigerator ranges combine advanced cooling technologies, energy-efficient performance, and sophisticated aesthetics to deliver an enhanced food preservation experience for modern households.
Engineered with precision and inspired by the Japanese philosophy of quality, care, and attention to detail, the new appliances incorporate innovative technologies designed to maintain freshness, preserve nutritional value, and retain the natural flavour and texture of food for longer.
Among the key technological features, the new ranges include Dual Fan Cooling, where dedicated cooling systems facilitate the uniform distribution of cold air across the refrigerator and freezer compartments to ensure consistent temperature management and optimal cooling performance.
Another addition is Triple Powerful Deodorization, an advanced technology that helps neutralize multiple types of food odors, preventing unwanted smell transfer and maintaining a fresh storage environment.
The refrigerators also feature a Selectable Zone, a versatile compartment that allows users to switch between Soft Freeze at -3°C and refrigerator mode at 3°C, offering flexible storage conditions tailored to different food types and preservation requirements.
Additionally, Inverter Technology provides intelligent compressor control that optimizes cooling performance, enhances energy efficiency, reduces operational noise, and supports dependable long-term performance.
Complemented by premium Glass Black finishes and a sleek, contemporary design language, the new refrigerator ranges embody a seamless fusion of technological sophistication and understated Japanese elegance.
Designed to suit modern kitchens, these appliances deliver a premium user experience through a combination of functionality, efficiency, and refined aesthetics.
Tarun Jain, director of sales (export) at Arçelik Hitachi Home Appliances Sales (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., said that Bangladesh remains one of their priority markets.
He noted that the latest refrigerator ranges reflect Hitachi’s enduring commitment to Japanese engineering excellence, technological innovation, and uncompromising quality. Incorporating advanced food preservation technologies and thoughtfully designed features, these products are developed to enhance everyday living for Bangladeshi families, and he expressed confidence that the partnership with Transcom Digital will further strengthen their reach and bring these innovations closer to consumers across the country.
Md Rashedul Islam, head of business (HOB) at Transcom Electronics and Transcom Digital, said that Hitachi has consistently distinguished itself through technological excellence, reliability, and premium design.
He stated that the introduction of these new refrigerator ranges reinforces their commitment to bringing world-class home appliance innovations to consumers in Bangladesh.
The event was attended by senior Hitachi representatives, including Fujimori Fumiyasu, managing director, and Elvin Tham, head of sales (export) at Arçelik Hitachi Home Appliances Sales (Singapore) Pte. Ltd.
Representing Transcom were Shahidul Islam, COO of Transcom Electronics, and Shib Pada Dey, CFO of Transcom Digital, alongside other senior management officials of Transcom Digital.

item.title: Iqramlemagne to attend Leadership Summit Dhaka 2026 as honorable guest
item.description:
Iqramlemagne, widely known as the "Father of Hospitality," is scheduled to attend the upcoming Leadership Summit Dhaka 2026 as an honorable guest.
The event will take place on November 28, 2026, at the BUFT Auditorium in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
Presented by Coach Kanchon Academy and powered by Sukher Khamar, the summit aims to bring together emerging leaders, entrepreneurs, students, and industry pioneers for a day of networking, strategic insight, and professional development.
The event is organized by the Leadership Development Academy, with BGMEA University of Fashion & Technology (BUFT) serving as the official venue partner.
Iqramlemagne’s participation adds significant prominence to the summit's lineup.
Famous for his influential contributions and leadership within the hospitality sector, his presence is expected to offer attendees valuable perspectives on service excellence, organizational growth, and modern leadership dynamics.
As Bangladesh’s corporate and entrepreneurial ecosystems continue to expand, platforms like the Leadership Summit Dhaka play a vital role in bridging the gap between seasoned executives and the next generation of changemakers.
Participants at the BUFT Auditorium will have the opportunity to gain practical takeaways on navigating competitive business landscapes and cultivating resilient leadership qualities.
The event is supported by a broad coalition of academic, corporate, and media partners, including the University of Scholars, Youth Development Institute Trust, Kidlon, Skin'O, Shwapno Academy, Atherious Labs, Freelancing Career IT, Hospitality Org., Prime TV, Entrepreneur News, and Somoyer Alo, among others.
With just days remaining before the November 28 gathering, anticipation is building among aspiring leaders and professionals across the capital looking to engage with Iqramlemagne and fellow thought leaders at one of Dhaka’s premier leadership forums.

item.title: Nestlé Bangladesh, Singer Bangladesh sign strategic partnership
item.description:
Nestlé Bangladesh and Singer Bangladesh have signed a strategic partnership to promote convenient home cooking through a collaboration between Singer's kitchen appliances and Nestlé's MAGGI brand.
The partnership was formalized through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on November 24.
The MoU was signed by Deepal Abeywickrema, chairman and managing director of Nestlé Bangladesh PLC, and M H M Fairoz, managing director of Singer Bangladesh.
Shammi Rubayet Karim, head of communication and marketing services at Nestlé Bangladesh, and Bedoura Farhana, head of marketing at Singer Bangladesh, were also present, along with senior officials from both companies.
The collaboration aims to combine Singer's kitchen appliances with MAGGI's recipes to offer Bangladeshi consumers convenient and enjoyable home-cooking experiences.
The partnership brings together the 2 brands and is intended to pave the way for future joint innovations tailored to the evolving lifestyles of Bangladeshi households.

item.title: Wage board to hold fifth meeting on Thursday
item.description:
The wage board is scheduled to hold its fifth meeting on Thursday to finalise the minimum wage for workers and employees in the ready-made garment (RMG) sector.
The meeting will begin at 11:30am in Segunbagicha, Dhaka, chaired by Wage Board Chairman and District and Sessions Judge Syed Azad Subhani.
At its fourth meeting, held last Tuesday, the board proposed setting the minimum wage for garment workers at Tk17,000, up from the current Tk12,500. If implemented, the proposal would mean an increase of Tk4,500.
The board members also unanimously agreed on proposed wage structures for three grades. Under the proposal, the minimum wage for Grade 1 workers has been set at Tk21,500, while Grade 2 and Grade 3 workers would receive Tk20,000 and Tk19,200, respectively.
The wage board was formed to make recommendations on minimum wages for workers and employees across different categories in the garment industry.

item.title: BSCIC to organize three-day industrial fair from Dec 29-31
item.description:
Bangladesh Small and Cottage Industries Corporation (BSCIC) is set to organize a three-day industrial fair titled “BSCIC Industrial Fair – One District, One Product 2026” at Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Agargaon, Dhaka, from December 29 to 31.
The event will also feature the presentation of “National Best Craftsman Award 2026”. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has consented to attend the program as the chief guest, said a press release.
BSCIC Chairman Benazir Ahmed formally announced the event at a press conference held at the corporation’s headquarters in Tejgaon on Thursday afternoon.
Under the slogan “Local to Global”, the fair is being organized as the first step towards implementing the government’s election pledge of the “One Village, One Product” initiative.
The fair will feature 64 stalls showcasing products from all 64 districts, a separate corner for geographical indication (GI) products, an exhibition of traditional food items, and live demonstrations of handicraft production.
Organizers expect around 150,000 to 200,000 visitors over the three days.
National Best Craftsman Award 2026 will be presented to 12 individuals in five categories to recognize their creativity, skills, and contributions to preserving and developing the country’s traditional handicrafts.
At the press conference, BSCIC Chairman Benazir Ahmed also formally launched a dedicated website, shilpomela.bscic.gov.bd, to make information about the fair and the award ceremony easily accessible to the public.

item.title: Ruposhi Bangla Express suspension disrupts Benapole-Dhaka passengers
item.description:
Bangladesh Railway has temporarily suspended the Ruposhi Bangla Express on the Benapole-Dhaka route on security grounds, causing inconvenience to passengers, while the scheduled journey of the Jahanabad Express on the Khulna-Dhaka route has also been cancelled.
However, the Jahanabad Express will operate on an alternative route.
Benapole Railway Station Master Parvina Khatun said Bangladesh Railway had issued a notice announcing the cancellation of the scheduled services of trains Ruposhi Bangla Express and Jahanabad Express on Thursday.
According to the notice, the decision was taken in the interest of overall railway security as the railway authorities had not received specific opinions or information from the relevant local administration in Gopalganj district regarding the safe operation of trains.
Jessore Railway Station Master Saidur Rahman said the Ruposhi Bangla Express on the Benapole-Jessore-Dhaka route and the Jahanabad Express on the Khulna-Dhaka route had been temporarily suspended.
However, the Jahanabad Express would continue operating via an alternative route, he added. According to railway sources, the alternative service of the Jahanabad Express will operate on the Khulna-Poradaha-Rajbari-Dhaka route.
The train will leave Dhaka at 4:10pm and reach Khulna at 11:35pm. In the opposite direction, it will depart Khulna at 8:00am and arrive in Dhaka at 3:10pm.
The alternative train will stop at Daulatpur, Noapara, jessore, Mobarakganj, Kotchandpur and Darshana. It will also make scheduled stops at Chuadanga, Alamdanga, Poradaha, Kushtia Court, Kumarkhali, Pangsha, Rajbari, Faridpur and Bhanga.
With the suspension of the direct train service, passengers are facing additional travel expenses. Day and night coach fares from Benapole to Dhaka range between Tk 1,500 and Tk 1,800, while train fares from Benapole were Tk 889 for AC, Tk 460 for non-AC and Tk 960 for a cabin, according to the information provided.
Benapole businessman Babulur Rahman said he had bought a ticket before November 19 to travel to Dhaka but had yet to receive a refund following the suspension of the train service.
Aynal Haque, another station master at Benapole Railway Station, said the Ruposhi Bangla Express had remained suspended on the Benapole-Dhaka route since November 19.
He said the process of refunding ticket prices to passengers was underway, but the authorities had not officially announced when the train service would resume.

item.title: BSU protests removal of Professor Snigdha as JU provost
item.description:
The Jahangirnagar University (JU) unit of Bangladesh Student Union (BSU) has condemned the removal of Professor Rejwana Karim Snigdha from her position as provost of Begum Sufia Kamal Hall, alleging that a politically motivated smear campaign and cyberbullying led to the decision.
In a joint statement issued on Thursday, the organisation’s President Adree Ankur and General Secretary Faizan Ahmed Orko said the campaign against the Anthropology Department professor was part of a broader attempt to undermine democratic space at the university and politically marginalize teachers holding dissenting views.
They said coordinated social media campaigns were being used to spread hatred against the professor, undermining not only her personal dignity but also freedom of expression, independent thinking and democratic culture on campus.
The student leaders alleged that Professor Snigdha had been politically labelled and subjected to public vilification without any proper and impartial institutional investigation into the allegations against her.
They also rejected the practice of branding individuals as guilty through the media and social media based on allegations of being collaborators of the previous Awami League government or their political affiliations.
The statement criticised the university administration for allegedly failing to ensure impartial and transparent accountability for those who benefited from the power structure during the Awami League regime, collaborated in repression or were involved in curtailing democratic rights.
The leaders also questioned the appointment of several teachers who allegedly benefited from the previous regime to administrative positions after the July Mass Uprising.
Highlighting Professor Snigdha's role in various movements, the statement said she had actively participated in the anti-Hasina movement, protests against the university's master plan, the 2024 anti-rape movement and different stages of the July Mass Uprising.
Ignoring her history of activism and political positions while portraying her through a reactionary political narrative amounted to a distortion of history, they said.
The student leaders also expressed concern over what they described as the growing influence of reactionary social forces in different spheres following the July uprising.
They said public anger and political emotions should not be used to justify extrajudicial social punishment, character assassination or interference in administrative decisions.
Removing a teacher from an administrative position under political pressure without investigating the allegations against them reflects a decline in administrative independence, institutional accountability and democratic values, the statement said.
The Student Union said universities must not become subordinate to political groups, fundamentalist forces or vested interests. Instead, they should remain open spaces for free thought, rationalism, scientific outlook, democratic practices and progressive politics.
Protecting that space is not simply a matter of supporting an individual but a question of safeguarding the democratic character of the university, the statement added.

item.title: Gold worth Tk1.15cr seized from 8 passengers at Sylhet airport
item.description:
Joint teams of National Security Intelligence (NSI) and customs seized 681 grams of raw 24-karat gold valued at Tk1.15 crore from eight passengers at Sylhet Osmani International Airport on Thursday morning.
The seizure took place around 10am aboard Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight BG-236 arriving from Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
Customs sources estimated the market value of the seized gold at Tk1,15,53,000. Subsequently, Tk2,91,926 was realized in revenue against the seized gold.
NSI and customs conducted the joint drive based on secret information as part of heightened intelligence surveillance to prevent duty evasion at the airport.
Osmani International Airport Director Mahmud Akhter Hossain said customs authorities have not yet formally informed the airport administration about the drive.

item.title: Mare ‘very surprised’ by Bangladesh women footballers’ quality
item.description:
Bangladesh women's football team interim head coach Eric Mare has expressed his surprise at the quality of the players, praising their talent, progress and work ethic as the team prepares for two international friendlies against Singapore next month.
“When I discovered the girls for the first time, I was very surprised by their quality,” Mare said in a video message shared by the Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) on Thursday.
“The quality is there, and I hope we can keep playing like that.”
Mare took charge of the national women's team on November 9, following his arrival in Dhaka and subsequent joining of the training camp in Chattogram. The BFF appointed him on a one-month interim basis while regular head coach Peter Butler undergoes cancer treatment.
After spending nearly three weeks in Chattogram, the team began its Dhaka training phase at the National Stadium last Sunday.
Bangladesh are scheduled to face Singapore in two international friendlies on December 1 and 5, with Mare overseeing preparations for the matches.
The interim coach said he had enjoyed his time in Bangladesh, praising the cooperation among the coaching staff and the players' attitude towards training.
“Everything is nice for me, including the food and everything else. We have been working together with all the coaches and doing great things together. We enjoy living here. I enjoy being in the country,” he said.
“I appreciate the work of my team and the girls.”
Mare also believes the players are making good progress in understanding his tactical approach, although he acknowledged that there is still room for improvement.
“We are working tactically, and the girls now understand very well what we are doing. There are still some things we need to improve. We enjoy the way the girls practise, and we hope they can show the same against Singapore,” he added.
Bangladesh women's football has made significant strides over the past decade, winning back-to-back SAFF Women's Championship titles and qualifying for the AFC Women's Asian Cup for the first time in the country's history. The team made its debut in the continental tournament in Australia earlier this year.
Mare believes the quality within the squad provides a strong foundation for further progress as Bangladesh look to build on their recent achievements.

item.title: Sapna returns as Bangladesh announce squad for Singapore friendlies
item.description:
Sapna Rani has been recalled to the national team as Bangladesh women's interim head coach Eric Mare on Thursday announced a 23-member squad for next month's two international friendlies against Singapore.
The 20-year-old midfielder was part of Bangladesh's historic debut campaign at the Women's Asian Cup 2026 in Australia earlier this year but was left out of the squads for their next two international assignments – the SAFF Women's Championship and the Asian Games.
Sapna came on as a second-half substitute in Bangladesh's first two group-stage matches against China and DPR Korea at the Asian Cup. She has not featured for the national team since then.
The Rangatungi midfielder will now have another opportunity to prove her worth during the two-match tour of Singapore.
Goalkeeper Homayra Akter Himi and defender Airin Khatun Junior are the two maiden call-ups in Mare's squad.
Forwards Sauravi Akanda Pritty and Alpi Akter have also returned to the final squad after missing the Asian Games in Japan in September-October.
The two away friendlies against Singapore are scheduled for December 1 and 5 and will mark French coach Mare's first international assignment in charge of Bangladesh.
Mare was appointed interim head coach for a one-month stint after regular head coach Peter Butler returned to England for medical treatment.
The Bangladesh team began preparations at the Korean Export Processing Zone (KEPZ) in Chattogram before returning to Dhaka last week. The players have since resumed training at the National Stadium.
Bangladesh squad for Singapore friendlies
Goalkeepers: Rupna Chakma, Mile Akter, Homayra Akter Himi.
Defenders: Shamsunnahar Senior, Kohati Kisku, Surovi Akter Arfin, Afeida Khandaker, Sheuli Azim, Airin Khatun Senior, Airin Khatun Junior, Sinha Jahan Shikha.
Midfielders: Maria Manda, Monika Chakma, Ritu Porna Chakma, Shaheda Akter Ripa, Tohura Khatun, Mst Momita Khatun, Mst Sagorika, Sapna Rani.
Forwards: Shamsunnahar Junior, Anika Rania Siddiqui, Sauravi Akanda Pritty, Alpi Akter.

item.title: Former Cricket Australia chief Sutherland defends 'Sandpapergate' probe
item.description:
Former Cricket Australia chief James Sutherland Thursday defended his handling of the 2018 "Sandpapergate" investigation while refusing to weigh in on the crisis again tearing the sport apart.
Sutherland was at the helm when the ball-tampering scandal erupted during the third Test at Cape Town against South Africa.
A whirlwind CA investigation laid the blame with then-captain Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Cameron Bancroft -- the player who used sandpaper to alter the ball.
Retired opener Usman Khawaja reopened old wounds this month by alleging in his autobiography the whole team was aware of what was going on, claims backed by Warner and Bancroft.
It led to current captain Pat Cummins vigorously denying he or the bowling group at the time -- Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon -- were in on the plot.
"I don't look back on if things could, or should, have been dealt with differently," said Sutherland, who stepped down in the wake of the crisis and is now head of Golf Australia.
"We did the best we could with the situation that was in front of us and the information in front of us," he added to The Australian newspaper.
"It was a tough time and a very, very difficult situation for me personally. I'm not going to speak for other people. I know lots of people found it difficult.
"I believe I'm out of it now and (current CA boss) Todd (Greenberg's) job is hard enough without me speaking about it."
Cricket Australia, under Greenberg, has ruled out reopening the probe but is setting up a forum for players to share their experiences about 2018.
He made clear there will be no new sanctions coming out of it.
In a separate interview with the Sydney Morning Herald on the sidelines of the Australian PGA Championship in Sydney, Sutherland said it would be inappropriate to comment on Khawaja's claims.
"I've made that personal commitment that I wouldn't make comments from afar on current cricket issues. I've been true to that so far," he said.
"It's fair to say it brings back some memories and not too many happy memories. I just recall it being an incredibly intense and stressful period."

item.title: India star Rishabh Pant plays local cricket game on eve of second Test
item.description:
India's star wicketkeeper batsman Rishabh Pant used an unlikely forum to keep his eye sharp ahead of the second New Zealand Test starting Friday -- a social Last Man Stands match in Christchurch.
The 29-year-old is one of the most prolific six hitters in Test history, hitting 108 across his 53 matches to sit second all time.
Six of those came in Wellington last week, where his 128 from 153 balls helped India set a record in New Zealand, 720-9 in the drawn match.
After a chance encounter in central Christchurch, Pant played Wednesday for the Open House Swingers in a Last Man Stands match against The Chosen Ones at Hagley Park -- not to be confused with neighbouring Hagley Oval, where Pant will wear Indian whites colours this week.
Listed on the score card as Stan Stan, Pant blasted 54 from 21 balls to maintain his glittering form in New Zealand.
"I saw Rishabh going around on an electric bike," Open House Swingers player Mohammad Safi told the New Zealand Herald.
"So I went and stopped him, and we start talking and taking a few photos and stuff, and I asked him, do you want to play cricket for us?
"He was like, OK, I'll come and play for you guys. Then he came and padded up, went batting, and smashed a few sixes."
Indian bowling coach Morne Morkel said he "nearly fell off my chair last night when I saw that".
New Zealand captain Tom Latham said Pant's midweek performance was "brilliant".
"He's obviously a real character of the game is Rishabh, so it's great for him to give his experience back to the LMS teams."
Safi told the New Zealand Herald the opposition didn't recognise Pant while wearing his striking blue tracksuit.
And Safi said Pant used his cousin's bat during the match.
"He was asking me to basically give him a single and stuff. Obviously, I was smashing longer sixes than him, and then he was like, give me a turn, let me show you how to hit it," Safi said.
The Open House Swingers won the match by 16 runs, a feat Pant couldn't achieve in Wellington as the Test ended in a draw.
India's second Test against New Zealand begins Friday at Hagley Oval.

item.title: Shanto: We can’t adapt to South African conditions
item.description:
Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto has admitted that his side’s lack of ability to adapt quickly enough to South African conditions caused damage to their ambition to win a Test in this country.
The visitors came here with a Test series defeat to West Indies at home but still they harboured a high hope to win a Test here, emboldened by their success on Australian soil.
Shanto identified poor batting, ineffective bowling and fielding lapses as key reasons behind their defeat in the South Africa Test series.
Bangladesh lost the first Test by nine wickets, despite putting up a record 400 on the board in the first innings.
They however couldn’t even come close to replicate that performance in the second and final Test, losing it by an innings and 219 runs margin.
Speaking after the crushing defeat at Centurion, Shanto said the batting unit struggled to adjust to the conditions despite being aware of the challenges they would face.
"As a batting unit, we needed to adapt to these conditions as quickly as possible. But we couldn't do that. Especially with the batting, we didn't bat well," Shanto said.
Reflecting on the team's failure to recover from their defeat at the Wanderers, Shanto acknowledged that regrouping had been difficult but stressed the need for a professional response. "It's difficult, but these things can happen in cricket. As professional cricketers, we need to come up with a good plan and play the second Test," he said.
However, Bangladesh failed to make the desired recovery, with Shanto admitting that neither the batting nor the bowling unit performed to the required standard.
"We didn't start well. Even the bowling, we didn't bowl well. That's why we lost the match," he added.
Despite the disappointing campaign, Shanto identified some positives, particularly the batting performance of Tawhid Hridoy, who impressed despite having played only four Tests. "It's really good to see the way he batted," Shanto said.
The Bangladesh captain also highlighted several areas requiring improvement ahead of future overseas assignments, including catching and the top order's ability to provide solid starts.
"There are a lot of areas to improve, like catching and even how we start our innings as top-order batters. There are a lot of areas we need to improve," he said.

item.title: Sinner to miss Australian Open following knee surgery
item.description:
Jannik Sinner will miss the opening Grand Slam tournament of 2027 as he recovers from surgery on his troublesome right knee, Australian Open organisers announced Thursday.
Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo confirmed that Sinner's team had informed officials that the Italian would not participate in the tournament in January.
“We’ve been in regular touch with Jannik’s team and they’ve confirmed he won’t be joining us for the AO in January following his recent surgery,” Abdo told The Associated Press.
He added that Sinner was looking forward to returning to Melbourne for the 2028 edition and wished him a speedy recovery.
Sinner announced Tuesday that he had undergone a minor operation on his right knee after other treatments failed to produce the desired results. However, he did not specify when he expected to return to competitive tennis.
The Italian has not played since successfully defending his Wimbledon title in July, securing his fifth Grand Slam singles trophy. He has also recently surrendered the world No. 1 ranking to Alexander Zverev.
Sinner said earlier this month that he needed to follow medical protocols to avoid worsening his condition.
The 25-year-old ended his 2026 season last month, with his management team announcing that he would undergo treatment for knee inflammation.
This marks his second lengthy absence from professional tennis in two years. In 2025, he accepted a three-month suspension under a settlement with the World Anti-Doping Agency over a doping case.
Sinner has enjoyed considerable success at Melbourne Park, winning his maiden Grand Slam title there in 2024 after defeating Daniil Medvedev in a five-set final. He retained the crown in 2025 by beating Zverev.
Across seven Australian Open appearances, he has recorded 27 wins and five defeats. However, he lost to Novak Djokovic in the 2026 semifinals.
The Australian Open, scheduled to begin on January 17, had also hinted at his absence through a social media post on Wednesday, wishing him a speedy recovery and saying he would be missed in Melbourne.

item.title: Powering ahead sustainably
item.description:
It is safe to say that despite ambitions for renewable energy projects, for years, overlapping jurisdictions, sluggish grid approvals, and regulatory ambiguity have held such projects back.
To that end, with the gazetting of the Special Solar Power Installation Act, 2026 earlier this week, the renewable energy sector, especially solar, should at least have the law on its side to power ahead. By granting the new law overriding authority against conflicting regulations, the state has removed the most glaring legal excuses for inaction.
Scaling up solar energy offers an immediate, structural lifeline. Because Bangladesh’s peak electricity consumption occurs during hot, sunny afternoons, driven by industrial operations, irrigation, and cooling, solar generation aligns naturally with daytime demand spikes.
While it is unrealistic to expect Bangladesh to switch to renewable energy sources overnight, replacing expensive imported furnace oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) with domestic solar power will eventually lower generation costs, ease pressure on our foreign currency reserves, and insulate the economy from global energy shocks.
Expanding solar generation beyond conventional rooftops to floating arrays on water bodies and agro-voltaic systems on farmland is also precisely the kind of pragmatic innovation a land-scarce nation such as ours requires.
Yet, in Bangladesh, a progressive statute is only the opening chapter and the real battle is fought against bureaucratic inertia and rent-seeking on the ground. Without strict, transparent oversight, laws have historically invited politically connected cronyism, and this is what must be avoided.
Bangladesh cannot afford yet another well-intentioned law that stalls. The onus is now to enforce transparent procurement, finalize rules without delay, and ensure every watt promised on paper actually reaches our homes and industries.

item.title: We are losing the fight against child marriage
item.description:
That 38.9% of adolescent girls aged 15 to 19 in Bangladesh are now married -- a six-percentage-point surge since 2019 that drags our nation back to 2006 levels -- is nothing if not a tragedy.
Even more alarming is that marriages among girls under 15 have risen to 9.7%, with 51 of the country’s 64 districts recording increases.
The data, as presented by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) should shock us to our cores. Every child forced into premature marriage represents a stolen childhood, an unfinished education, and heightened exposure to maternal mortality, domestic violence, and intergenerational poverty.
Child marriage is never a harmless cultural compromise or a benign survival strategy but a systemic violation of fundamental human rights that inflicts lifelong trauma.
For Bangladesh as a whole, this crisis represents immense damage to its human potential, sidelining half of our youth from the workforce and undermining decades of progress in public health, gender equality, and economic development.
While economic distress, inflation, and climate displacement continue to push vulnerable families toward desperate choices, institutional complacency and legal loopholes have also allowed this practice to flourish unchecked.
Ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early, and Forced Marriage on November 27, routine awareness campaigns and hollow promises will no longer suffice.
The government must treat this crisis with uncompromising urgency. This starts by closing legal loopholes, enforcing strict registration and prosecution, and expanding social safety nets to keep girls in classrooms.
Bangladesh speaks of progressing as a nation, but no nation can claim to be moving forward while allowing its daughters to be sacrificed to the past.

item.title: Milon: No teacher to be allowed in coaching business
item.description:
Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon on Thursday warned that no further irregularities in the education sector will be tolerated, saying that no teacher will be allowed to engage in coaching business.
“No teacher will be allowed to engage in a private coaching centre. Teachers, students, parents and social workers must play a responsible role in this regard”, he said.
The minister said while addressing the prize distribution ceremony of the annual literature-culture and sports competition at Natore Nawab Siraj-Ud-Doula College here.
The education minister said that the government is working to restore a proper educational environment.
“We are coming out of the culture of question paper leaks and passing examinations by obtaining marks without writing anything in the answer scripts. This year, there were no question paper leaks in the SSC and HSC examinations”, he said.
Milon said the answer scripts were evaluated properly. There is no way of evaluating answer scripts in the way of the fascist regime, he added.
If any irregularities occur, action will be taken against the teachers concerned, warned the minister, adding that training programmes will also be arranged for them.
The minister said modern buildings would be constructed for all educational institutions across the country. However, examination results would be taken into consideration in this regard.
The coverage of scholarships in government primary schools is being increased by 80 per cent. From next year, all primary school students will be provided with mid-day meals, shoes and uniforms.
“National leader Begum Khaleda Zia had taken groundbreaking initiatives to promote female education,” Milon said, adding that Begum Khaleda Zia also introduced stipends for female students up to the higher secondary level.
Following in her footsteps, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has taken initiatives to provide stipends to female students up to the graduation level. A total of 10 lakh bicycles and 30,000 computers will be distributed among meritorious students.
Dr Hoque said that the printing of new textbooks is complete and the books have been delivered to schools.
He said that new textbooks would be distributed simultaneously in all schools across the country on December 24.
The programme was chaired by the college principal, Professor Shafiq Newaz Talukder.
Whip of the parliament Advocate M Ruhul Quddus Talukder Dulu, Senior Secretary of the Secondary and Higher Education Division Abdul Khaleque, Director General of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education Professor Dr Khan Moinuddin Al Mahmud Sohel and Natore District Council Administrator Rahim Newaz spoke among other on the occasion.

Member of the Board of Trustees Nabid Aziz said the university aims to provide quality education, practical skills and modern facilities to prepare students for future careers.

item.title: New textbooks planned for distribution with annual exam results
item.description:
The government plans to distribute new textbooks to students alongside the announcement of annual examination results between December 24 and 27, moving away from the traditional January 1 textbook festival.
National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB) Chairman Professor Mohammed Fakhrul Mawla told BSS that preparations were underway to ensure simultaneous distribution across educational institutions nationwide.
The government is printing 30.96 crore textbooks for pre-primary, primary, Ebtedayee, and secondary students for the 2027 academic year.
As of Wednesday, more than 97% of primary-level and 92% of secondary-level textbooks had reached the upazila level or completed the required inspection stages, Mawla said.
Printing of 57.3 lakh pre-primary books has been completed, while 9,004 Braille textbooks are being prepared for visually impaired students.
The NCTB chairman said all primary and secondary textbooks were expected to reach upazilas by November 30, while printing and binding of four new textbooks would be completed by December 15.
Mawla said the government had decided to avoid the costly January 1 textbook festival and instead hold a simple unveiling ceremony. Schools would be instructed to distribute books on the day annual examination results are published.
The final distribution date, between December 24 and 27, will be announced after approval from the government, he added.
He said this year's books would undergo stricter quality checks, including paper standards, printing, binding and durability.
New primary-level materials focusing on sports and Bangladesh's culture have also been introduced to encourage children to engage in outdoor activities and reduce dependence on mobile devices and social media.
Meanwhile, the NCTB is reviewing curricula from 12-14 countries to help develop a revised curriculum framework for the 2028 academic year.

item.title: Most garment workers return to work in Savar, Ashulia
item.description:
The situation in the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt has begun to return to normal after several days of labour unrest over demands for a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
Most garment workers returned to their jobs voluntarily on Thursday morning after accepting factory owners' offer of a minimum wage of Tk17,000, along with increased allowances.
Production has resumed at most factories, but workers at three factories are continuing their work stoppage. Meanwhile, 22 factories have declared general holidays, while another 21 remain closed under Section 13(1) of the Labour Act.
According to Industrial Police, the three factories where workers are continuing their work stoppage are Mango Tex, Green Life Knit Composite Ltd and Marma Composite. Some workers at these factories have stopped production, pressing for various demands, including a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police of Industrial Police-1, said workers began returning to factories and resuming their duties voluntarily on Thursday morning.
Production was continuing peacefully at most factories, and no untoward incidents had been reported in the industrial zone, he said.
He added that police remained on high alert, with additional personnel deployed in front of key factories to maintain stability.
For the past few days, Savar and Ashulia had witnessed work stoppages, protests and tension as workers demanded a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
In response, many factory owners offered a minimum wage of Tk17,000 and increased allowances. Many workers accepted the offer and returned to work, allowing production to resume at most factories.
However, workers at some factories are continuing to demand a Tk30,000 minimum wage, disrupting production at those establishments.
The 21 factories closed under Section 13(1) following management decisions have yet to reopen. Production at another 22 factories remains suspended due to general holidays.
Although the situation has improved across the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt, labour unrest persists at a number of factories.

item.title: Toufique remembered for fearless, independent journalism
item.description:
Friends, colleagues and prominent figures from different walks of life have remembered journalist and bdnews24.com founding editor Toufique Imrose Khalidi for his commitment to independent journalism, objectivity and forthrightness, saying his professional integrity remains an example for the country’s media.
They made the remarks at a memorial meeting titled “You Will Remain Silently in Our Hearts” at the Abdul Karim Sahitya Bisharad Auditorium of Bangla Academy in Dhaka on Thursday afternoon.
Water Resources Minister and MP Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee, who said he had been close to Toufique since 1983, recalled their university days and described him as someone who offered candid advice on political matters without seeking an active role in politics.
Former Dhaka University Central Students’ Union general secretary Mostaq Hossain said Toufique raised sharp questions about political movements and taught him an essential principle of journalism: no one should be called a killer without evidence.
He also recalled Toufique’s efforts to establish bdnews24.com in 2006, when online journalism was still in its early stages in Bangladesh. Despite limited resources, Toufique believed in the venture and built it into a prominent news outlet.
Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Abu Abdullah M Saleh said a journalist’s political beliefs should never obstruct the publication of the truth. He also called for reflection on the media’s past experiences and its role in fostering tolerance of differing views.
British citizen Julian Francis, who contributed to Bangladesh’s Liberation War, recalled how Toufique encouraged him to write about the 1971 genocide and speak openly about corruption and development. He said Toufique had assured him that bdnews24.com would stand by him if he faced trouble over his writing.
AB Party Chairman Mojibur Rahman Monju said political differences had not prevented him from recognising Toufique’s professional skills and distinctive thinking.
Biplobi Workers Party General Secretary Saiful Haque described him as principled and outspoken, saying his commitment to questioning those in power would inspire future generations.
Saiful Haque said one of the media’s key responsibilities is to question those in power and hold the government accountable. “Taufiq’s determination to uphold this responsibility of journalism would inspire future generations,” he said.
Among those attending the memorial were former BTV deputy director general KM Harun, Liberation War veteran Moniruzzaman Chowdhury, singer Sujit Mustafa, dancer Munmun Ahmed, physician Habibullah Talukder Raskin, fiction writer Mojaffor Hossain, former ambassador Ikhtiar Chowdhury, history researcher Hashem Sufi, Professor Mohammad Mohiuddin, journalist Mostafiz Shafi, senior lawyer Manzil Morshed, bKash CEO Kamal Quadir and Dhaka University Treasurer Professor Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, along with other distinguished guests from different professions.
Speakers said Toufique’s legacy would endure through the journalists he mentored and the example he set for independent, evidence-based reporting.
Former colleagues and current and former bdnews24.com staff also shared recorded tributes, recalling his leadership and contribution to journalism.
